idiom_name: Spring Kafka DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer on the JVM; coroutine Channel only for in-process staging
implementation_notes: Kotlin inherits the JVM frameworks: Spring Kafka's DefaultErrorHandler with DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer moves records to a dead-letter topic, and the conversion exceptions (DeserializationException, MessageConversionException, ConversionException) are fatal by default - they skip retries and reach the recoverer on the first failure. Kotlin's own idioms carry the validation: sealed hierarchies plus exhaustive when give a compile-time-checked decoder. A kotlinx.coroutines Channel(capacity) is the invalid-message channel only inside one process - it is an in-memory staging buffer, not a durable destination - so it should not stand in for the framework's DLT when the message crosses a process boundary.
pitfalls: A coroutine Channel loses its contents on restart, so using it as the invalid channel for brokered messages breaks the diagnostic promise of the pattern.
Platform types from Java interop (String!) hide the distinction between absent and null, so a validation that compiles can still let invalid payloads through to the handler.
Cancelling the listener scope (shutdown, rebalance) can abort an in-flight DLT publication unless the routing step runs in a non-cancellable context.
